prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Draw ONE NEW finished webcomic panel, not a poster, collage, split board or multiple panels. SQUARE image, requested 1024x1024.
Reference 1 is the original drawing/world benchmark. Reference 2 supplies only our newly inspected cast identities, clothing and equipment. Compose the completely new moment described below. Do not reproduce either reference's framing or add its absent characters.
Reference 3 is ONLY an editable geometry/contact schematic. Preserve its useful force/contact relationships but draw the specified camera, realistic anatomy, faces and medium from references 1–2. Never render its labels, stick figures, colored debug shapes or diagram background. C-head has two jaw countercontacts, clear exit beside implement, dry support and connected water body. Not just a hook pulling lower jaw.
Drawing treatment: Strong black brush masses, scraped white edges and controlled grayscale planes, limited hot-magenta institutional lights. Graphic ink narrative with selective rough marks. Preserve Adult face character, monumental flood infrastructure, black umbrella-segment creature and dry wit under genuine threat. Avoid Glossy leather everywhere, repetitive white water sparkles, polished wet mirror floor, decorative ink splatter over clues.
World context: Monumental concrete floodworks. Dry elevated inspection ledge on LEFT, black canal two meters below RIGHT; one broad spillway gap and a tall locked sluice with a magenta signal panel. Water uses large black/white shape groups.
VISIBLE subjects in this panel ONLY:
Corin Vey: Light-skinned adult man, lean strong build, angular tired face, short black hair with gray temple, faint stubble. Off-white long coat over charcoal high-neck shirt and belted black combat trousers; flat black boots. Equipment: One long straight iron ward-pole with a broad simple solid C-shaped head: upper shoulder can prop an upper jaw while lower curve catches lower lip. No moving mechanism. Held in both hands when fighting. Small plain black notebook kept inside coat.
Lio Marr: Light-skinned adult man, short dark hair, narrow face, pale rolled-sleeve work shirt, dark trousers, plain boots. Unconscious when first physically seen, then breathing and shaken. Equipment: Small brass municipal sluice key on a cord at neck.
Umbrella eel: One thick black segmented canal creature with overlapping umbrella-like membrane ribs, tapering body and broad hinged pale mouth. Two large readable gripping jaws, no human limbs. Equipment: Its wet body moves through connected water; it cannot propel its full weight across the dry high ledge.
Inspected reference qualification for visible subjects only: Corin currently has a BARE LEFT hand and a plain black glove on his RIGHT hand. Lio’s municipal key has a simple TRIANGULAR brass head, not the round bow in the sheet.
Visibility/cropping constraints: lio: only readable portions inside mouth opening; FL09 includes one wet boot heel, pale sleeve and hand. Do not duplicate a full body outside mouth.
ONE current moment: He leans back with the ward-pole and brings the lower jaw onto the dry ledge lip. The C-head’s upper shoulder physically props the upper jaw while its lower curve retains the lower lip; the far side remains an open exit. The heavy trunk slides against the wall below.
Current physical state (authoritative): Pole acts as a physical two-contact jaw prop, both hand grips maintained. Lower jaw rests on concrete edge; C-head upper shoulder holds upper jaw away. Trunk in water; Lio sleeve visible through unobstructed far-side exit.
Special visual element, only if specified: none
Camera and framing: Wide side full force chain: boots, torso, pole, jaw, ledge and water. Respect actual subject-to-frame size, especially extreme wides. Do not enlarge a distant person into a medium shot.
Reserve the upper 35% of the image as calm, broad in-world background for later speech balloons. Keep ALL faces, hands, important contact and clue details BELOW that zone. Do not draw balloons or text; the blank space will receive editable lettering.
Draw acting with a specific expression and body intention. For contact, show the physical source/contact/target and its immediate reaction. For a clasp or weapon, make shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand-object ownership legible. Keep supports, scale and visible limb anatomy sound. Do not add later injuries, additional duplicates, alternate weapons, generic glows or undescribed consequences.
Surface design: matte quiet ground, broad deliberate light and shadow shapes, selective purposeful architecture. Group foliage, hair and material marks. Keep medium-defining directional ink/brushwork; avoid pervasive microtexture, repeated tiny facets, flooring crack networks, mirror floors and reflection glitter. Preserve richness through faces, composition and world depth.
No text of any kind, no speech balloons, no glyphs, no captions, no SFX lettering, no UI, no signatures, no watermark, no frame. Exact dialogue will be added separately. Return only the new artwork.
